name: Sister Anwen
greeting: Mind the cup on the step. The man from the south road needs it more than I need a clean floor.
lines: Kael: Three people missing?
Anwen: Bram drove. Sella had Oren beside her. He left his coat here because the sun was out.
Anwen: Take the north road into Wychwood. Look for their cart, then bring me what you find. They have people waiting here.
Anwen: They found old wooden tokens where the road was being repaired. Sella asked me to read one. I did.
Kael: What happened when you read it?
Anwen: The candles went out. I sent them away while I found a rite I thought would keep them safe.
Anwen: If you find red thread around black feathers, keep it intact. I tied it. I owe you that much before you go.

variants.greeting: Thank you for the water. Now, the three who have not come home.
I have put the grain list beside the burial book. No one has to sign one to receive the other.
lines: Anwen: I could call that a beginning. It is mostly a table and two people willing to sit at it.
Kael: Beginnings usually look smaller when somebody is doing the work.

variants.greeting: I will give you the register. You said you would not demand my oath. I am still not agreeing to stand in the rite.
lines: Kael: The record can speak to facts. It cannot make your promise for you.
Anwen: Then you do understand the difference.

variants.greeting: Edric wants my hand on the new seal. He has already counted the households that cannot afford to refuse.
lines: Anwen: The old rite borrowed consent from frightened people. That is why it keeps breaking.
Kael: Can the Hart be released without making everyone here swear?
Anwen: Yes. Someone must freely keep the recovered account. One person can begin. More people can share the work.

variants.greeting: Three strokes. A burial, a restored name, and a promise that has stopped holding.
lines: Anwen: I cut the rope last winter. A novice heard an erased name and walked into the sealed chapel. I found him too late.
Kael: You closed it again.
Anwen: Yes. I told myself I was buying time. The graves will show what that time cost.

actions.label: I'll stay until the people carrying this can speak safely.
actions.result: Kael: I cannot promise nobody gets hurt. I can promise I will not take the coin and leave you to it.

actions.label: I'll stay. We keep a record nobody can close again.
actions.result: Kael: Copies, names, living witnesses. Not another secret that depends on one person.

actions.label: I'll stay, but you tell me what you are asking me to carry.
actions.result: Anwen: That is fair. I should have asked before I put the token in your hand.

variants.greeting: You brought the account to me. We can speak here without putting anyone's name on the board.

lines.text: Anwen: That is Oren's carving. Turn it over. The older name is beneath his paint.
Anwen: That burial thread is mine. I thought it would quiet what they were carrying.
Kael: Someone bound it again with Vargan wire. I found the binding on the road.

lines: Kael: The pack is dead. The people hiding this are alive.
Anwen: Take your payment if you must. I need help I have no right to order.

lines: Kael: People needed to know what was on their road.
Anwen: Yes. And the people who can explain it need a way to survive being known.
Kael: Then we do both. I will not leave the second part to a notice.

variants.greeting: Keep the originals if you need to. We can work from the account you choose to share.

lines.text: Anwen: Oren painted over a refugee's token. Sella wanted the first name restored.
Kael: Someone alive left drag marks beside the creatures' tracks.

lines: Anwen: Then leaving now would leave a witness carrying something dangerous. I am asking you to stay.
